Terminal States

Terminal States

Understand explicitly declared states with no outgoing transitions and the limits they place on further workflow state changes.

Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

This document defines States with no outgoing Transitions in their Workflow definition.

Requirements

  • WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-001 — A Workflow definition MUST explicitly identify each terminal State.
    Evidence & context1 research note+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Preventing an invalid state does not guarantee eventual completion ↗

    Acep Taryana; Dieky Adzkiya; Muhammad Syifa’ul Mufid; Imam Mukhlash

    Valid transitions, intentional terminal states and non-mutating rejection do not establish fairness or per-request eventual completion. The hospital study supplies methodological context, not financial execution evidence or a universal deadline.

    Scope and limitations

    This is methodological transfer from healthcare, not a financial rule demonstrated by that study. Fairness, resource availability and admissible requests matter. An intentionally terminal state is not a deadlock defect; statistical confidence is not an unconditional proof for arbitrary executions.

  • WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-002 — A terminal State MUST NOT have an outgoing Transition in that Workflow definition.
  • WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-003 — A Transition Request from a terminal State MUST fail with FINKORE_WORKFLOW_TERMINAL_STATE.
  • WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-004 — Terminal status MUST be determined from the Workflow definition, not inferred from naming.

Invariants

Once a Workflow instance enters a terminal State, no further Transition in that Workflow definition must succeed.

Examples

APPROVED and REJECTED may both be terminal states even though their domain outcomes differ.

Invalid Examples

Treating a state named COMPLETE as terminal without declaring it terminal is invalid.

Errors

An ordinary transition from a terminal state must report FINKORE_WORKFLOW_TERMINAL_STATE.

Non-Goals

This document does not determine whether entity fields or operational metadata become immutable in a terminal State; see Entity Mutability. It also does not define Correction, Reversal, Void, Cancellation, Supersession, or Adjustment behavior.
